text: Welcome to Salesforce Data Model Fundamentals. Before anything else in this course makes sense, you need one concept cold: the object. This lesson is just about that one word.

Three words get used constantly, and they're easy to mix up at first. An object is the table itself, like Account. A field is one column in that table, like Phone or Industry. A record is one row of real, saved data, like the actual company Acme Corporation.

Here's something familiar to anchor it: a spreadsheet of properties. Columns for Price, Bedrooms, Bathrooms, Square Footage. Every row is one property for sale. That's the shape of an object, before Salesforce is even involved.

Now the same data, as an actual Salesforce record. Property is the object. Price, Bedrooms, and Square Footage are fields on it. This one record, two ninety eight Castle Street, is one row — one saved instance of that shape.

Here's a second Property record, a different address entirely. Notice it has the exact same fields as the first one, just different values. That consistency is the whole point of an object: it defines a shape every record of that type has to follow.
Object, field, record. Keep those three straight and the rest of this chapter is just filling in detail. Next up: the standard objects Salesforce gives you before you customize anything.
